title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 107
paragraphs: Of those who were conquered by the Greeks, Xerxes reckoned no one a man of worth except Boges, who was at Eion; him he never ceased praising, and he paid very high honor to his children who survived him in Persia. Boges indeed proved worthy of great praise. When he was being besieged by the Athenians under Cimon son of Miltiades, and could have come out under a truce and returned home to Asia, he chose not to do so, for fear the king might think he had survived through cowardice; instead, he held out to the last. When there were no longer any provisions within the wall, he heaped up a great pyre, cut the throats of his children, his wife, his concubines and his servants, and threw them into the fire; after that he scattered all the gold and silver of the city from the wall into the river Strymon, and having done so, he threw himself into the fire. For this reason he is justly praised by the Persians to this day.
